prompt:
Find what the Debian project officially states about the support period of a stable release, including LTS. Cite the Debian page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Debian project officially defines the support period for a stable release as lasting until the next stable release is made, plus an additional period covered by the Long Term Support (LTS) team. Specifically, the standard support lasts for approximately one year after the next release, and LTS extends this by an additional two years for specific architectures.

SOURCE: https://www.debian.org/support | QUOTE: "Each stable release is supported for about one year after the next stable release has been made." | CLAIM: The standard support period for a Debian stable release ends approximately one year after the subsequent stable release is issued.

SOURCE: https://wiki.debian.org/LTS | QUOTE: "Debian LTS extends the lifetime of Debian stable releases by 2 years beyond the end of life of the regular security team support." | CLAIM: The Long Term Support (LTS) project extends the support period for Debian stable releases by an additional two years after the regular security support ends.
